title: Cell Biology & Biomolecules
confusion: ❌ 'Prokaryotes lack all organelles.' ✅ They lack *membrane-bound* organelles (nucleus, mitochondria), but possess non-membrane-bound organelles like ribosomes.
❌ 'Nucleotide and nucleoside are the same.' ✅ Nucleotide = Nucleoside (sugar + base) + Phosphate. Nucleoside lacks the phosphate group.
❌ 'Enzymes are consumed in the reaction.' ✅ Enzymes are catalysts; they speed up reactions by lowering activation energy but are NOT consumed (they are regenerated).
❌ 'Mitochondria are purely eukaryotic.' ✅ While found in eukaryotes, their circular DNA and structure suggest an endosymbiotic origin related to prokaryotes.
notes: **Cell theory:** all living organisms are composed of cells; the cell is the structural and functional unit of life; all cells arise from pre-existing cells (Schleiden, Schwann, Virchow).
**Prokaryotic vs eukaryotic cells:** prokaryotes lack a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles (bacteria); eukaryotes have a nucleus and organelles such as mitochondria, ER, Golgi bodies.
**Mitochondrion:** powerhouse of the cell — site of aerobic respiration and ATP synthesis; has its own circular DNA (semi-autonomous organelle).

**Biomolecules:** carbohydrates (energy source; glucose C₆H₁₂O₆), proteins (made of amino acids joined by peptide bonds), lipids (fats/oils; concentrated energy store), nucleic acids (DNA/RNA carry hereditary information).
**Enzymes** are globular protein catalysts that speed up biochemical reactions by lowering activation energy; they are substrate-specific and work best at optimum temperature and pH.
